comparison: Both evaluations support the severe iDKO phenotype with histology, flow cytometry, and fertility data. OpenEval emphasizes multiple independent lines of evidence (C63-C74, C97, C60-C61, C75) while peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'morphological data on atrophy and arrest of spermatocyte meiosis are solid.' Both include overlapping claims about meiotic arrest (C97-C103 in OpenEval R2 also covered in peer R1), showing strong concordance on core phenotypic findings.

OpenEval R2 focuses specifically on meiotic arrest evidence (C97-C105) using flow cytometry and immunofluorescence. Peer R1 includes these same meiotic arrest claims (C97-C103) within a broader evaluation of reproductive phenotypes. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with strong agreement on the pachytene arrest conclusion.

OpenEval R3 addresses Leydig cell dysfunction with emphasis on scRNA-seq, immunofluorescence, Western blot, and hormone measurements (C5-C7, C110-C116, C161-C167). Peer R2 focuses narrowly on hormone measurements (C5-C6, C165-C167) and accepts testosterone loss without challenging the broader molecular data. Both SUPPORTED, but OpenEval provides more comprehensive mechanistic evaluation.

Both evaluations support the transcriptomic findings on steroidogenic gene downregulation. OpenEval R3 emphasizes multiple orthogonal approaches (scRNA-seq C110-C116, immunofluorescence C161, Western blot C163, hormones C5-C7) while peer R3 affirms 'high resolution of molecular defects' from single-cell RNA-seq. Strong concordance on data quality and correlation with steroid biosynthesis disruption.

Perfect claim overlap (C13-C15, C80-C82, C194, C257) on CCNC depletion data. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and accept the Western blot evidence showing CCNC loss in iDKO but not single knockouts. However, peer reviewers note this observation alone doesn't fully support the mechanistic conclusions about kinase-independent function, showing slight divergence in interpretation of implications.

Major disagreement on kinase inhibitor evidence (C11-C12, C177-C178, C180, C183, C259, C261). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, emphasizing multiple lines of evidence including in vivo treatment, drug concentration validation, and ex vivo studies. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly critiquing 'no controls for effective target inhibition shown.' This represents the most significant concordance gap in the entire analysis.

Significant disagreement on the kinase-independent mechanism conclusion (C18, C184, C262). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while acknowledging the inference remains speculative. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating the claim 'is interesting but was not supported by the data presented' and criticizing lack of definitive experiments. Both recognize limitations but differ substantially in confidence level.

Both evaluations support Sertoli cell dysfunction findings (C137-C148 in OpenEval, C137-C146 in peer). OpenEval emphasizes scRNA-seq combined with immunofluorescence and GO analysis, rating evidence as strong. Peer reviewers accept the findings and note they are 'interesting' and 'could be investigated further,' showing agreement on data quality with interest in deeper characterization.

Perfect claim overlap (C150-C153, C156-C158) on spermatocyte gene expression analysis. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and affirm the scRNA-seq data quality showing predominantly upregulated DEGs. OpenEval notes the 99.2% upregulation pattern is consistent with CDK8/19 as negative regulators, while peer reviewers accept this as 'high resolution of molecular defects.' Strong concordance.

Both evaluations support the temporal recovery data (C172-C176, C239-C242). OpenEval emphasizes the partial nature of recovery and lack of CYP17A1 restoration as ruling out incomplete knockout. Peer reviewers accept these observations without challenge, treating them as factual findings. Both acknowledge the mechanism remains speculative. Strong agreement on data validity.

Both address CDK8/19 spatial expression (C89-C92) using IHC. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, emphasizing differential localization and complementary spatial/quantitative data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, specifically requesting clarification about the 'completely distinct' locations in different cells and what this means for double knockout interpretation. Disagreement on whether spatial data are adequately explained.

Perfect claim overlap (C58-C59, C61-C62, C76-C77, C204) on CDK8 single knockout infertility. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and accept the behavioral infertility without morphological defects. Peer reviewers note the finding is 'surprising' and suggest more detailed characterization needed, while OpenEval notes the mechanism remains unexplored. Agreement on validity with shared recognition of incomplete understanding.

OpenEval R12 evaluates differential compensation between tissues (C84-C85) as SUPPORTED, noting this explains mild single knockout phenotypes and supports functional redundancy. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing tissue-specific compensation patterns.

Perfect claim overlap (C86-C87, C198-C199) on pSTAT1 as a pharmacodynamic marker. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and accept the finding that pSTAT1 does not correlate with CDK8/19 knockout. This methodological insight about activity assessment is accepted without critique by both evaluations, showing complete concordance.

Perfect claim overlap (C53-C54, C200-C201) on intestinal phenotype. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and accept the histological findings. Peer reviewers note a minor unaddressed query about counting methodology but accept the overall finding. OpenEval emphasizes this validates the iDKO model approach. Strong concordance with minor methodological clarification suggested.

OpenEval R15 evaluates ex vivo Leydig cell culture data (C10, C181, C251) as SUPPORTED, noting cell-autonomous effects but acknowledging small sample sizes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing the ex vivo validation experiments.

OpenEval R16 evaluates lipid accumulation data (C170-C171, C253) as SUPPORTED, using comparison to StAR knockout to support impaired steroidogenesis interpretation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing the Oil Red O staining findings.

OpenEval R17 evaluates CDK19 single knockout mild phenotype (C33, C56-C57) as SUPPORTED, establishing baseline for comparison. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing CDK19 iKO fertility and health observations.
